subject.title: memory_search: chokidar file watcher silently stops delivering events, index goes stale

question: Should unconfigured memory search start a default periodic sync fallback for existing users, or should periodic sync remain opt-in while the watcher failure is handled another way?
rationale: Defaulting `memorySearch.sync.intervalMinutes` from disabled to non-zero changes background indexing/provider behavior for existing setups, which is a product and upgrade-safety choice rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Accept default-on fallback after PR repair
options.body: Merge the linked fix path once the interval dirty behavior is scoped correctly and explicit `intervalMinutes: 0` remains the opt-out.

options.title: Keep periodic sync opt-in
options.body: Leave the default at 0 and document `intervalMinutes: 30` plus `openclaw memory index --force` as the supported recovery path until a different watcher-health design is chosen.

options.title: Rework around watcher health
options.body: Pause the default change and pursue watcher diagnostics, restart/health checks, or doctor guidance instead of changing the sync default.

recommendation.title: Accept default-on fallback after PR repair
recommendation.body: Merge the linked fix path once the interval dirty behavior is scoped correctly and explicit `intervalMinutes: 0` remains the opt-out.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory-search config/docs path history makes this the best available owner for the default and upgrade-behavior decision.
